summary: Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology and completed doctoral studies under Pallab Sengupta. In 2026, Chakrabarty is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at SOAS, CNRS, and the International Association for Tibetan Studies.

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University. He was headmaster at Bramham College, examined Buddhist Chinese books for the India Office Records, and served as professor at University College London.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds from around 1927 to 1930 and served on the faculty at the University of Manchester from circa 1951 to 1971.
Samuel Johnson worked in linguistics and related fields. He was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (around 1725–1726), and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).

Samuel M. Grupper works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Wells Williams worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute around 1831–1832 and held an academic post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and also held a post at the same institution.
Sandra Hochwarter works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Anne MacDonald.
Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under the supervision of Sanghasen Singh. In 1995, Sun is attested as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College.

Sangay Dorji works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, Dorji later taught at Semtokha Rigney School and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004).

Sangharakshita was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Chien Ming Chen, and Dhardo Rinpoche. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (circa 2013–2017) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 2018–2020).

Sangye Tenzin was a scholar and practitioner in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery and was attested as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia.

Sanjay Subrahmanyam is a historian who studied at the University of Delhi, including St. Stephen's College and the Delhi School of Economics. He held chairs and teaching posts at EHESS, the University of Oxford, Collège de France, and UCLA.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under M. K. Ganguli and A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati University, and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held academic posts at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, Jadavpur University, Utrecht University, and the University of Oxford.
Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Leiden University between approximately 2015 and 2021 under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhaddanta Narada and at Harvard University. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
